newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait fuel stations sale won't hit prices.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait fuel stations sale won't hit prices.

text.p: Kuwait's Oil Minister said in remarks published on Saturday a plan to privatise 30 filling stations will not affect petrol prices.
"Fuel prices will not rise after privatisation," al-Watan newspaper quoted Isa al-Mazeedi as saying.
"The Supreme Petroleum Council will impose strict monitoring on the prices of petrol in privatsied stations," he added.
The state-owned Kuwait National Petroleum Co (KNPC), in charge of local marketing of oil products, sells gasoline locally at a subsidised price of 40-50 fils ($0.13-0.16) per litre.

In February, the Council approved a plan to privatise 30 of some 80 state-owned petrol stations serving the two million population of the oil-rich Gulf Arab state. Kuwait has no private sector petrol stations.
Mazeedi said under the plan the state will establish a shareholder firm of whose shares it will retain 25 percent and put the rest in a public offering.
Mazeedi did not give a timetable for the plan, but he said it would be under a trial period of 6-8 years.

The state, trying to give a larger role to the private sector in the state-orchestrated economy, is still in the early stages of executing a wide-ranging privatistion plan that includes water, electricity and telecommunications.
Since 1994 Kuwait has sold stake worth over $2.0 billion in local firms in the first phase of a privatisation plan.
Kuwait hopes to gain parliamentary approval in 1997 to start the next and more difficult stage of privatising public utilities.
However, officials say major oil industry function -- production and refining -- are not part of privatisation plans.
